source_excerpt: Replacing $q$ by $-q$ we may assume $B$ is positive definite, and completing the square $q(w)=(w-w_0)^TB(w-w_0)+v$. Let $\mu_1,\mu_2>0$ be the eigenvalues of $B$ with orthonormal eigenvectors $e_1,e_2$. The map $(\delta,\theta)\mapsto w_0+\sqrt{\delta/\mu_1}\cos\theta\,e_1+\sqrt{\delta/\mu_2}\sin\theta\,e_2$ is a diffeomorphism of $(0,\infty)\times[0,2\pi)$ onto $\R^2\setminus\{w_0\}$ with $q=v+\delta$ and Jacobian $1/(2\sqrt{\det B})$. Hence $q(W)$ has density $(2\sqrt{\det B})^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}p_W(w(\delta,\theta))\dd\theta\le\pi L/\sqrt{\det B}$ at $v+\delta$, and density zero below $v$. This is a change of variables in a deterministic integral; no independence after rotation is used.
